title: HF datasets cache: each runner.os key needs exactly one saving job; consumers set restore-only
answers: CI hits Hugging Face 429 rate limits when fetching datasets
how do I make a job read the shared hf datasets cache without writing it
Windows Hugging Face datasets cache never gets saved
body:
Symptom: CI jobs fetch Hugging Face datasets anew and get rate limited (429), or the shared datasets cache for one platform never gets populated.
Root cause: .github/actions/cache-hf/action.yml:runs.steps uses actions/cache, which also saves the cache when the job ends, so every caller of the composite writes the key.
Fix pattern: The `restore-only` input (default "false") makes the composite use actions/cache/restore instead, gated by `if: inputs.restore-only == 'true'`. Set `with: restore-only: true` on consumer jobs such as .github/workflows/protobuf-cross-test.yml and .github/workflows/test-requirements.yml.
Constraints: The key is `${{ runner.os }}-hf-datasets-<hash>`, so each OS needs its own saver. master.yml (ubuntu-latest) is the only Linux writer. The Windows job in .github/workflows/slow-tests.yml must stay save-enabled because it is the only writer of the Windows key; restore-only there means that key is never populated. Before marking a caller restore-only, confirm another job saves the same runner.os key.
applies: Any workflow that calls .github/actions/cache-hf, on any runner OS.
says: Automated test runs are hitting rate limits when downloading external datasets.
Windows test builds never cache shared datasets and download them repeatedly every run.
Prevent consumer build jobs from overwriting the shared dataset cache during pipeline runs.
Continuous integration jobs are failing because dataset requests receive too many requests errors.
Share downloaded datasets across pull request checks to avoid reaching external download limits.
search: In .github/actions/cache-hf, each runner.os cache key requires exactly one saving job while consumer workflows must configure restore-only. Because actions/cache saves on job completion, consumer jobs like .github/workflows/protobuf-cross-test.yml and .github/workflows/test-requirements.yml should pass restore-only: true to invoke actions/cache/restore instead. Each operating system has a separate ${{ runner.os }}-hf-datasets-<hash> key; .github/workflows/master.yml on ubuntu-latest is the sole Linux saver, while the Windows job in .github/workflows/slow-tests.yml must retain cache saving. Setting restore-only on a runner OS without an existing saver prevents its cache from ever being populated, leading to Hugging Face 429 rate limit errors.
